summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, severe headache, and back pain following a lumbar puncture three weeks prior. Her symptoms were attributed to a gastroparesis flare and migraine exacerbation, possibly worsened by dehydration and muscle tension. She had leukocytosis on admission that resolved, and Group B Strep was found in urine without symptoms, deemed asymptomatic. Peritoneal fluid showed no signs of infection. She was treated with IV anti-nausea medication, erythromycin for gastroparesis, uptitrated topiramate for migraines, and short-term oxycodone for pain. Her oral intake improved, vital signs stabilized, and she was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for pain management and integrative medicine.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
